# Behavioral Specification: KMAC Application Interface

## 1. Purpose

This module acts as the front-end interface between software, one or more hardware application interfaces, and the KMAC/SHA3 datapath. It selects which source owns the message path, forwards the correct message data and control commands, selects the secret-key source and configuration, and routes the resulting digest or Keccak state to the correct consumer.

The module does not perform hashing itself. It must ensure that only one operation owner is active at a time, that application operations are isolated from software operations, and that secret-key or internal-state information is not exposed to the wrong interface.

## 2. Configuration Model

The module is compiled with a fixed number of application interfaces. Each application interface has a static configuration that defines:

- Whether the application operation is KMAC or SHA3.
- The Keccak security strength to use.
- Whether the application uses its own prefix or the software-programmed prefix.
- The application-specific prefix value, if used.
- The application digest width.

The digest width must be one of the supported KMAC/SHA3 output widths. The width of the sideloaded secret key is assumed to match the application digest width.

The module may be built with masking enabled or disabled. When masking is enabled, secret-key, digest, and Keccak-state paths carry two shares. When masking is disabled, a single share is used, and any second-share output shall be zero.

## 3. Operation Ownership and Arbitration

When the module is idle, it shall accept either a software Start command or a message beat from an application interface. The first request that arrives determines the owner of the operation.

If an application request and a software Start command are presented at the same time, the application request shall take precedence.

Once an operation is owned by one source, ownership is exclusive:

- During an application-owned operation, software message data shall be discarded, and software commands other than Start shall be reported as errors. A software Start command shall be ignored.
- During a software-owned operation, application requests shall be ignored. No application interface shall be granted ready, and no application digest or done response shall be generated.

At the end of an operation, the module shall return to idle and be ready to accept a new request.

## 4. Application-Initiated Operations

### 4.1 Start and Configuration

When an application interface is granted ownership, the module shall use that application’s configuration for the entire operation.

If the application uses KMAC, the sideloaded secret key must be valid. If the key is not valid when the operation is about to start, the module shall:

- Not start the hashing operation.
- Report a key-not-valid error condition.
- Enter an error state and remain there until reset.

If the application uses SHA3 only, an invalid sideloaded key shall not prevent the operation.

### 4.2 Message Transfer

After the application configuration has been accepted, the module shall accept message beats from the selected application interface.

Only the selected application interface shall receive a ready indication. All other application interfaces shall see no ready and shall not have their data forwarded.

The message transfer ends when a message beat marked as the last beat is accepted. The module shall not infer the end of an application message from any other condition.

### 4.3 Automatic Output-Length Insertion

For an application-owned KMAC operation, the module shall append the KMAC right-encoded output length after the last message beat. The output length corresponds to the configured application digest width.

This encoded output length shall be inserted as an additional message beat before the hashing operation is commanded to process.

For an application-owned SHA3 operation, no output-length insertion is performed. The module proceeds directly to process after the last message beat.

### 4.4 Process and Completion

After the application message and, if required, the output-length value have been delivered, the module shall command the hashing datapath to process the message.

When the hashing datapath indicates that the message has been absorbed, the module shall:

- Present the resulting digest to the selected application interface.
- Assert a done indication to the selected application interface.
- Issue the corresponding done command to the hashing datapath.
- Return to idle.

The digest shall be truncated to the configured application digest width. When masking is enabled, the digest shall be provided in two shares. When masking is disabled, the first share shall contain the unmasked digest value and the second share shall be zero.

Only the selected application interface shall receive the digest and done indication. No other application interface shall receive them.

## 5. Software-Initiated Operations

### 5.1 Start Command

A software operation begins with a Start command issued while the module is idle. This command shall be forwarded to the hashing datapath to begin the operation.

If software presents message data before Start is issued, that data shall be discarded and an error shall be reported.

### 5.2 Software Message Transfer

While the software owns the operation, software message beats shall be forwarded to the message datapath together with their byte-level mask.

The module shall remain in software mode until the software explicitly issues a Done command.

### 5.3 Software Commands

While in software mode, the module shall forward software commands to the hashing datapath unchanged. This includes Process, Run, and Done.

- Process commands the hashing datapath to finalize the message.
- Run commands the hashing datapath to perform an additional Keccak permutation when a longer output is required.
- Done terminates the software operation and returns the module to idle.

For a software-initiated KMAC operation, software is responsible for appending the KMAC right-encoded output length to the message before issuing Process. The module shall not insert it automatically.

### 5.4 Software Status

When the software owns the operation, the module shall forward the hashing datapath’s absorbed indication to the software status path. This indicates that the absorbing step is complete and that the Keccak state is available for reading or further processing.

This status shall not be forwarded during an application-owned operation.

## 6. Message Datapath Behavior

The message output shall carry both data and a byte-level mask so that partial-word message writes can be represented.

- For software-sourced data, the provided byte mask is passed through.
- For application-sourced data, byte strobes shall be expanded to the same per-byte mask format.

When no source is selected, the message output shall be inactive, with no data and no mask asserted.

The selected source shall be granted readiness only while the downstream consumer can accept the beat. If the selected source is not ready, the module shall not advance the operation past that beat.

## 7. Secret-Key Handling

The module selects the secret key from two possible sources:

- The software-programmed secret key.
- The hardware sideloaded secret key.

For a software-owned operation:

- If sideloading is disabled, the software-programmed key and software-programmed key length shall be used.
- If sideloading is enabled, the sideloaded key shall be used, and the key length shall be the fixed length matching the application digest width.

For an application-owned operation, the sideloaded key shall always be used, and the key length shall be the fixed length matching the application digest width. This applies regardless of the software sideload-enable setting.

When masking is disabled, the two shares of the sideloaded key shall be combined into a single unmasked key value. When masking is enabled, the two shares shall be preserved and passed through without combining.

## 8. Prefix and Configuration Outputs

The module drives the hashing configuration outputs, including the prefix, KMAC enable, SHA3 mode, and Keccak strength.

For a software-owned operation:

- The prefix shall be the software-programmed prefix.
- KMAC enable, SHA3 mode, and Keccak strength shall be taken from the software configuration.

For an application-owned operation:

- The prefix shall be selected according to the application’s prefix-mode configuration. If enabled, the application-specific prefix is used; otherwise, the software-programmed prefix is used.
- KMAC enable shall be set if the application mode is KMAC and cleared if it is SHA3.
- The SHA3 mode shall be cSHAKE for KMAC application mode and SHA3 for SHA3 application mode.
- The Keccak strength shall be taken from the selected application’s configuration.

After an application operation completes, the module shall restore the software-programmed configuration outputs. A software configuration change made during an application operation shall not affect that operation and shall take effect only after the operation completes.

## 9. Keccak State and Digest Visibility

The software-visible Keccak state output shall be active only while a software-owned operation is active. At all other times, including application-owned operations, the state output shall be invalid and all state data outputs shall be zero.

This requirement prevents internal state values from an application operation, or from a KMAC operation using a sideloaded key, from being exposed to software.

For application-owned operations, the digest is derived from the Keccak state and returned only to the selected application interface. The digest is presented only with the application done indication.

## 10. Error Reporting

The module shall detect and report the following local error conditions:

- An application-owned KMAC operation attempted while the sideloaded key is not valid.
- Software message data presented while no software-owned operation is active.
- A software command other than Start or None issued while no software-owned operation is active.

When one of these conditions occurs, the module shall report a corresponding error indication and shall not allow the invalid operation to affect the active message datapath.

If the hashing datapath reports an error during an application-owned operation, the module shall reflect that error on the selected application’s response. Core-reported errors are otherwise not converted into local protocol errors by this module.

If multiple local error conditions occur at the same time, the module shall report one deterministic error. Software-interface protocol errors take precedence over state-transition errors.

## 11. Reset and Idle Behavior

On reset, the module shall:

- Return to idle.
- Select no active application operation.
- Clear any latched application selection.
- Present the software-programmed configuration outputs.

In idle, the module shall not accept message data. It shall remain ready to accept either an application request or a software Start command, subject to the arbitration rules above.
